item.title: Decoupling the Intrinsic Li/Mn Disorder Mechanism in Li-Rich Layered Oxides
item.description:
این کار وجود بی‌نظمی درون‌لایه‌ای Li/Mn در دامنه‌های Li2MnO3 را تأیید کرده و با DFT نشان می‌دهد پیکربندی‌های Li-excess و TM-excess به‌طور مکمل redox آنیونی را تقویت و چارچوب را پایدار می‌کنند.
Nano Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in confirming intrinsic intralayer Li/Mn disorder within Li2MnO3 domains, classified as Li-excess and TM-excess configurations. Significance: DFT reveals complementary roles—Li-excess promotes oxygen redox activity, TM-excess stabilizes TM–O bonding and framework. Coupling these configurations enables more reversible anionic redox, suppresses oxygen release and TM migration, improving electrochemical stability of Li-rich cathodes.
🏷 Li-rich layered oxides · Li/Mn disorder · anionic redox · Li2MnO3 domains · DFT calculations

item.title: Reaction-Programmed Interphase Reconstruction by an Ultrathin Zinc Phosphate Nanofilm for Reversible Lithium Metal Anodes
item.description:
نانوفیلم نازک zinc phosphate به عنوان پیش‌ماده واکنشی، در حین آبکاری Li ساختار بین‌سطحی را بازسازی کرده و با ایجاد سایت‌های lithiophilic و فاز Li3PO4-rich، رسوب یکنواخت و پایداری آند lithium را بهبود می‌دهد.
Nano Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in an ultrathin zinc phosphate nanofilm that reconstructs during initial lithiation into Zn and a Li₃PO₄-rich phase, integrating nucleation regulation and interphase protection in one precursor layer. This enables dendrite-free, compact Li deposition, low overpotential, and stable cycling over 1400 h, improving LiFePO₄, NCM811, and sulfur full cells—offering a simple, scalable route to reversible Li metal anodes.
🏷 zinc phosphate nanofilm · lithium metal anode · interphase reconstruction · lithiophilic Zn alloy · nucleation regulation

💡 This study provides the first in situ nanoscale visualization of stripping-induced failure in aqueous zinc batteries, categorizing residual zinc into four distinct pathways. It reveals crystallographically selective dissolution (Zn(100)/Zn(101) over Zn(002)) as a key degradation mechanism, establishing stripping—not just plating—as critical to reversibility and offering kinetic modulation strategies for improved battery longevity.

item.title: An Aqueous Phase Transition Electrolyte Retaining High Ionic Conductivity after Solidification for Low-Temperature Zinc–Iodine Batteries
item.description:
یک الکترولیت گذار فازی آبی با حفظ رسانایی یونی بالا پس از انجماد، چرخه‌پذیری فوق‌العاده باتری Zn||I2 را در دمای پایین ممکن کرد.
Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a phase-transition electrolyte that, unlike anti-freezing strategies, retains high ionic conductivity after solidification via an interconnected ice framework with continuous liquid pathways. This enables 1.870 mS cm⁻¹ at −60 °C and record 430,000-cycle Zn||I₂ battery life at −40 °C, shifting the paradigm from preventing freezing to sustaining ion transport in the solid state.
